## Summary

GitHub Feed plugin installation succeeds, but direct installs remain disabled in the runtime. Enabling them only in VS Code leaves canvas contributions unavailable. Browse can also show a separate installed row and fail to resolve uninstall after the runtime reports a different name.

- Route profile-level plugin enablement through the owning runtime, verify the persisted state, and reload live chats. Keep workspace overrides local and preserve managed-policy enforcement.
- Confirm **Install and Enable**, activate the exact discovered feed installation, and report partial installation/activation failures explicitly. Allow direct plugins in `/plugin` enable/disable commands and completions.
- Use stable direct-source identity for Browse reconciliation and uninstall. Preserve catalog names/icons, reconstruct associations after restart, keep marketplace copies separate, and disable ambiguous/unavailable uninstall actions with an accessible explanation.
- Surface plugin/extension reload errors returned by the runtime.

Uses existing runtime APIs; no runtime dependency or remote protocol changes.

## Manual verification

The reporter manually verified both automatic activation and the subsequent Browse identity fixes in Code OSS. Reproduction/verification steps:

1. Install Token Pacman from GitHub Feed and confirm **Install and Enable**.
2. Verify VS Code and runtime enablement, and use the canvas without restarting the chat.
3. Search Browse and confirm the installed feed item retains its catalog presentation rather than appearing as a second temporary-name entry.
4. Restart, uninstall, and reinstall; verify the same installation is targeted. A separately installed marketplace copy should remain independent.
5. Toggle profile enablement and verify runtime state and live contributions update.

Created as a draft as requested; automatic activation and Browse identity fixes are manually verified. The branch contains one change commit and is currently 10 commits behind main; refreshing upstream was blocked by local Git pack/object errors. No rebase was performed.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed UI-to-Agent-Host call path, T×S call count, per-chat serialization, cross-chat parallelism, and MCP restart capability are all explicit in repository code. Exact reload duration and typical live-chat count are unmeasured, which limits severity but not mechanism confidence.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Per-session plugins.reload IPC calls and the MCP server subprocess restarts they can trigger
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For T profile enablement changes while S chats are live, the new path performs T×S session reloads, in addition to three root plugin RPCs per change. Reloads run in parallel across chats but serialize in each chat's queue, so a burst leaves S queues with T expensive reloads each.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased plugin-management latency, blocked chat queues, and repeated CPU/subprocess churn from restarting plugin MCP servers
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Profile enablement actions only wrote the local enablement model; they did not cross into the Agent Host or reload any live SDK sessions.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each profile enable/disable now performs list, enable/disable, and verification RPCs, then awaits a queued plugins.reload for every live session. The management bridge starts mutations immediately, and the list UI disables only the clicked row, so changing several plugins can enqueue overlapping mutations without any shared reload coalescing.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added RIGHT line 3065 introduces the all-live-session loop on every setPluginEnabled call; before this PR profile actions called enablementModel.setEnabled locally and had no reload loop.
Findings.Title: Coalesce plugin reloads across profile changes
Findings.Impact: Managing several plugins in the installed list, or overlapping automatic activation with another toggle, queues one full plugin reload per change in every open chat. Since reloadPlugins explicitly notes that it can restart MCP servers and uses the same per-chat queue as chat control work, settings actions and subsequent chat work wait behind repeated restarts.
Findings.Evidence: setPluginEnabled ends with Promise.all over _allLiveSessions(), queuing reloadPluginEnablement for every session. _allLiveSessions returns every live chat entry; _queueChat serializes work only within one session, not across mutations; AgentHostManagementService._runMutation invokes each operation immediately. PluginListWidget disables only the selected toggle, allowing other rows to start additional changes. CopilotAgentSession.reloadPlugins calls the session plugins.reload RPC and documents that it can restart MCP servers.
Findings.Recommendation: Coalesce pending profile mutations into a shared flush: apply the requested enable/disable updates, then schedule at most one queued reload per live session for the burst and have all callers await that shared reload/error result. Preserve workspace-only changes as local operations.

Scenarios.Scenario: Toggle one or several installed plugins at profile scope
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The row/action awaits setAgentPluginEnablement, the browser-to-Agent-Host management call, two runtime inventory reads around enable/disable, and plugins.reload in every live chat before the local profile decision is committed and the clicked control is re-enabled. The reload work is on the user-visible settings critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke Agent Host setPluginEnabled from the workbench process
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Profile changes wrote the local enablement model without crossing the process boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before local enablement is published

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Runtime plugins.list, plugins.enable/disable, then plugins.list verification
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three serial runtime calls per profile change
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No runtime plugin calls occurred for workbench profile toggles.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All three must finish before session reloads begin

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Session plugins.reload, which can restart plugin MCP servers
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call for every live chat per profile change; T×S after a burst
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No live sessions were reloaded by workbench profile toggles.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All live-session reload promises are awaited; queued chat work waits behind each session's reloads

Scenarios.ScalingInput: T profile changes and S live chats. Effective cardinality is T management calls, 3T root plugin RPCs, and T×S session reloads; workspace-scoped changes bypass the runtime path.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: AgentHostManagementService starts mutations immediately. Different row toggles can overlap; each live chat's _queueChat serializes its T reloads, while the S chat queues run concurrently. There is no shared reload coalescer or aggregate limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or negative cache participates. Every profile change lists installed plugins before and after mutation and reloads every live session regardless of a concurrent pending reload.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the UI call chain, immediate mutation admission, all-live-session loop, per-chat serialization, and reload's MCP restart behavior are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical live-chat count and MCP restart duration are not measured, so severity is medium; the multiplicative call count and blocking behavior are certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable missing coalescing: multiple realistic row changes enqueue repeated expensive reloads in every live chat.

Scenarios.Scenario: Install and automatically activate a catalog plugin
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the existing SDK applyInstall completes, the new flow waits for discovered plugin identity (up to 10 seconds), then awaits the same profile enablement transaction and all-live-chat reload before reporting install success.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One apply call per confirmed install
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The install flow already awaited applyInstall.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh installed plugin config, resolve the plugin directory, and read its manifest during discovery
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced discovery refresh after installed state changes, with bounded reads per installed plugin
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Discovery still occurred after installation, but install completion did not wait for it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The diff newly waits for the matching discovered plugin before activation; timeout is 10 seconds

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enable the installed plugin and reload all live sessions
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three root plugin RPCs plus S session reloads
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Catalog install returned after apply and left the plugin disabled.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected plugin, P discovered plugins scanned on each discovery update, and S live chats reloaded once. Pending/catalog association storage remains capped at 1000 entries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Discovery is driven by a 200 ms coalescing scheduler for installed-plugin state. Once identity resolves, reloads run concurrently across S chat queues and serialize with any work already queued in each chat.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Installed-plugin state is cached and equality-checked by CopilotCliInstalledPluginsStore; positive discovery is observed, while timeout is not cached. Catalog associations and receipt sessions are bounded.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the changed critical path and boundary count.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Discovery and reload duration depend on filesystem/runtime state; this single-operation path is intentional for Install and Enable.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: the one-time discovery wait and reload are required by the new explicit activation behavior; concurrent activation reloads are covered by the reported coalescing issue.

Scenarios.Scenario: Uninstall an installed plugin while multiple chats are live
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The flow re-reads plugin inventory to resolve exact identity, performs uninstall through the owning runtime, then awaits reload attempts for every live chat before returning.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List runtime plugin installations for mutation-time identity resolution
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The provider already re-read inventory before uninstall.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One uninstall call through either the selected live session or root client
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The selected session or root client performed the uninstall.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reload plugins in every live chat
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: S session reloads for one uninstall
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A selected live session reloaded only itself; root uninstall did not reload live chats.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The operation waits for all attempts

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One installation lookup over N installed plugins and S live chats; reload cardinality is S after grouping by live SDK session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All S reloads are admitted together and each uses its chat queue. Promises.settled waits for peer reloads even if one fails; there is no aggregate limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The displayed identity is not trusted for mutation, so inventory is re-read. Catalog associations are deleted on success and bounded to 1000; no reload cache applies.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for S-way fan-out and concurrency.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Live-chat and MCP-server counts vary. Uninstall is an infrequent explicit operation and each live session needs reconciliation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: it is a single required reconciliation event rather than repeated work under a common trigger; the aggregate reload concern overlaps the reported enablement mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Refresh Browse installed-state reconciliation after plugin discovery changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: An actual top-level plugin discovery change now raises provider onDidChange; the install service refreshes provider installations, then synchronously reconciles installed resources for the next observable snapshot. This is off the direct typing path after the 200 ms installed-state coalescer.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read Copilot CLI installed plugin state after a watched config change
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per 200 ms coalesced burst; unchanged content emits no discovery change
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The installed-plugin discovery already watched and read this state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Feeds asynchronous discovery rather than blocking catalog typing directly

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh runtime plugin inventory and SDK customization installation receipts
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider refresh after each effective top-level plugin discovery change
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Plugin discovery changes alone did not request provider inventory refresh.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N runtime plugin installations, P discovered plugins, and up to K=1000 known catalog resources. Reconciliation includes N scans over P discovered plugins and matching against known resources.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Installed-plugin config file events are coalesced for 200 ms and unchanged snapshots are suppressed. Provider refresh versions discard stale results, though underlying refresh calls can overlap if distinct events occur.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Installed plugin config has a positive cache with structural equality suppression. Receipt sessions are capped at 50; known resources, catalog associations, and pending associations are capped at 1000. Provider inventory is always refreshed on a real discovery change.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the added event-to-refresh path and bounded state.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical plugin/catalog counts are unknown, but file events are coalesced and equality-filtered.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: refreshes correspond to effective installed-plugin state changes, are coalesced, and retained maps are bounded.

Scenarios.Scenario: Enable or disable a direct-source plugin with the /plugin command
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The live session lists plugins, toggles the direct source ID, and reloads that same session before producing command output.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three session runtime calls per explicit direct-source command
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Direct-source commands were rejected before runtime calls; marketplace plugin commands already used the same boundary pattern.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One explicitly selected plugin and one current live session per command.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The command runs in its session command flow; one reload follows one mutation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache; plugin inventory is read once to resolve ambiguity. This matches the pre-existing marketplace command behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Runtime durations vary, but cardinality is fixed at one plugin and one session.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: newly supported direct-source behavior uses the existing bounded command pattern without collection fan-out.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all 36 changed files and all diff pages. One introduced regression was reported: uncoalesced profile enablement changes multiply expensive plugin reloads across every live chat. Other changed boundary fan-out is tied to single explicit install/uninstall operations or coalesced discovery changes and did not independently meet the reporting threshold.
